chief_complaint: sudden painful red lump on eyelid margin with tenderness and pustule (Hordeolum / Stye)
hpi_details: 28F presents with 3-day history of a painful, swollen, red bump on the upper eyelid margin of her left eye. Feels like a tender pimple on the edge of her eyelid where her eyelashes grow. Yesterday noticed a small yellowish point of pus developing at the base of an eyelash. Eye feels gritty when blinking, but vision is perfectly clear and eyeball itself is white and non-tender.
ideas: thinks she caught a bacterial infection from old mascara
concerns: bothered by tender swelling and unsightly pimple on her eyelid
expectations: wants quick-acting antibiotic drops or draining so she can wear makeup to an event

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Hordeolum (stye) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes conservative warm compress therapy and lid hygiene, with topical antibiotics reserved for persistent infection, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: sudden painful red lump on eyelid margin with tenderness and pustule (Hordeolum / Stye)

Key HPI features: 28F presents with 3-day history of a painful, swollen, red bump on the upper eyelid margin of her left eye. Feels like a tender pimple on the edge of her eyelid where her eyelashes grow. Yesterday noticed a small yellowish point of pus developing at the base of an eyelash. Eye feels gritty when blinking, but vision is perfectly clear and eyeball itself is white and non-tender.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: HR 72, Temp 36.6C. Visual acuity 20/20 bilaterally. Eyelid exam reveals a localized 4 mm erythematous, indurated, exquisitely tender nodule on the anterior upper left eyelid margin centered around an eyelash follicle (Zeis/Moll gland obstruction), demonstrating a small central focal yellowish pustule pointing toward the skin. Conjunctiva is mildly injected locally near the lid margin, but the cornea is crystal clear and extraocular movements are full without orbital pain.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Hordeolum (stye).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Chalazion without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Spreading redness beyond the lid margin would suggest cellulitis.
management_principles: Conservative warm compress therapy (First line): instruct patient to apply clean, warm, moist compresses over the closed left eyelid for 10-15 minutes, 4 times daily combined with gentle lid margin massage to liquefy sebum and promote spontaneous drainage

Hygiene instructions: strictly advise against squeezing, popping, or lancing the stye at home (prevents spreading infection into orbital septum); discard old eye cosmetics and avoid contact lenses during infection
Topical antibiotic ointment: prescribe Erythromycin or Bacitracin ophthalmic ointment applied to lid margin BID for 7 days
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: 28F presenting with localized, acute, painful erythematous nodule at the eyelash follicle margin characteristic of External Hordeolum (Stye).
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: HR 72, Temp 36.6C. Visual acuity 20/20 bilaterally. Eyelid exam reveals a localized 4 mm erythematous, indurated, exquisitely tender nodule on the anterior upper left eyelid margin centered around an eyelash follicle (Zeis/Moll gland obstruction), demonstrating a small central focal yellowish pustule pointing toward the skin. Conjunctiva is mildly injected locally near the lid margin, but the cornea is crystal clear and extraocular movements are full without orbital pain.
reference_soap.assessment: Acute External Hordeolum (Stye) of the Left Upper Eyelid margin, secondary to localized Staphylococcus aureus follicular infection.
reference_soap.plan: 1. Conservative warm compress therapy (First line): instruct patient to apply clean, warm, moist compresses over the closed left eyelid for 10-15 minutes, 4 times daily combined with gentle lid margin massage to liquefy sebum and promote spontaneous drainage. 2. Hygiene instructions: strictly advise against squeezing, popping, or lancing the stye at home (prevents spreading infection into orbital septum); discard old eye cosmetics and avoid contact lenses during infection. 3. Topical antibiotic ointment: prescribe Erythromycin or Bacitracin ophthalmic ointment applied to lid margin BID for 7 days. (If fails to drain after 2-3 weeks and consolidates into a painless hard rubbery nodule, diagnosis transitions to Chalazion requiring elective ophthalmology incision and curettage).

learning_objectives: Differentiate Hordeolum / Stye (acute, PAINFUL, erythematous infectious abscess of eyelash follicle/Zeis gland or Meibomian gland caused by S. aureus) from Chalazion (chronic, PAINLESS, firm rubbery granulomatous lipogranuloma of blocked Meibomian gland)
Recommend first-line conservative management consisting of aggressive warm moist compresses applied 4 times daily to liquefy glandular secretions and promote spontaneous drainage
Explain why mechanical expression, squeezing, or popping of eyelid margin infections must be avoided to prevent retrograde spread into preseptal/orbital cellulitis
Outline indications for elective surgical incision and curettage or intralesional steroid injection for chronic consolidated chalazia that fail conservative warm compress therapy after 3-4 weeks

teaching.one_liner: 28F with a 3-day painful, red, swollen bump on the eyelid margin with a developing pustule.
red_flags: Spreading redness beyond the lid margin would suggest cellulitis

must_ask.say: Can you show me where the bump is and how painful it feels?
Have you noticed a small yellow or white point forming?
Is the redness spreading beyond the eyelid, or is your vision affected?
Do you regularly use eye makeup, and how old are your products?

must_ask.objective: Explain warm compress therapy and no-squeeze rule
must_ask.say: Apply warm compresses 4 times a day, and please don't squeeze or pop it.

history.answer: I have a painful, swollen red bump on my left upper eyelid that started a few days ago. Yesterday, it started looking like a little pimple with a yellow head right where my eyelashes grow.
It started three days ago as a tender red spot on my left upper eyelid. It gradually got more swollen and sore, and then the yellow pimple head showed up yesterday.
The redness is only right along the edge of my left upper eyelid where the bump is. The white part of my eyeball itself is clear and normal.
The bump itself is really tender and throbs if I touch it. It also feels gritty, like there is an eyelash or sand in my eye every time I blink.
No, my vision is completely fine and not blurry at all. I can see just as clearly as usual out of both eyes.
No, normal light does not bother or hurt my eyes at all.
No, I haven't seen any halos or rainbows around lights. I don't have a headache or any nausea either.
I had a tiny bit of dried crust along my lashes when I woke up, but there is no continuous pus or thick discharge leaking from my eye.
No, it does not itch at all. It just feels sore, swollen, and tender.
There is a swollen, tender red lump right on the margin of my left upper eyelid. It hasn't spread to my whole eye or cheek.
Yes, yesterday morning I noticed a tiny yellowish spot of pus forming right at the root of one of my eyelashes.
No, the redness and swelling are staying right around that one spot on my eyelid. My whole face and cheek look completely normal.
No, moving my eyes in any direction does not hurt at all. My eye isn't bulging out either.

history.answer: No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or body aches.

I do wear eyeliner and mascara every day. Honestly, I've been using an old tube of mascara that is several months past its expiration date.
No, I don't wear contact lenses. I only wear reading glasses occasionally when working at my computer.
No, I didn't get hit in the eye, and no chemicals, dust, or sparks splashed into it.
No, I don't have seasonal allergies, hay fever, asthma, or eczema.
I work as an accountant, so I look at computer screens all day, but my eyes aren't usually dry or irritated. This feels completely different from eye strain.
No, I don't have any morning back stiffness, joint pain, mouth ulcers, or bowel problems.
No, I've never had cold sores, shingles, or any water blisters on my forehead or nose.
No, I don't take blood thinners. I haven't had severe coughing spells, vomiting, or heavy lifting.

I suspect I gave myself a bacterial infection by using that old mascara tube.

I have a big family event this weekend, so I'm really worried about how red and unsightly this pimple looks. I'm hoping to get some fast-acting antibiotic drops or have it drained so I can wear makeup.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, or thyroid issues.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 116/74 mmHg, heart rate is 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 14 breaths per minute, body temperature is 36.6 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
The patient is comfortable and in no acute distress, with visible localized swelling along the left upper eyelid margin.

Visual acuity is 20/20 in both eyes; extraocular movements are full without pain; pupils are equal, round, and reactive; anterior left upper eyelid margin shows a 4 mm tender erythematous nodule centered on an eyelash follicle with a focal central yellowish pustule; upper eyelid eversion reveals no foreign body.
Mild localized injection of the bulbar conjunctiva adjacent to the left upper lid margin; remainder of conjunctiva and sclera is white, and the cornea is clear without abrasions or opacity.
No tenderness on palpation over the maxillary sinuses, frontal sinuses, or the left lacrimal sac area.
No palpable lymphadenopathy in the preauricular, submandibular, or cervical lymph node chains.
Surrounding periorbital and facial skin is intact with no spreading erythema, warmth, induration, or vesicular rash.
Cranial nerves II through XII are grossly intact with symmetrical facial sensation and expression.
